triage.reasoning: INV-B output is -58.4% versus expected, and string B-17-S3 shows a -58.4% deviation while the array deviation is -41.71% with 5 of 7 strings faulted. The cell temperature of 65.6 C exceeds the fleet median of 62.8 C, indicating an abnormal loss condition.
triage.verificationRationale: Both heavy localized soiling and physical cell damage (a cracked cell driving its bypass diode into conduction) can produce the observed string‑level loss and temperature rise; only visual and thermal imaging can differentiate them.

prognosis.degradationMechanism: Bypass‑diode conduction creates a contiguous hot row, raising cell temperature above the 65 °C propagation threshold; sustained exposure at the forecasted 67.5 °C accelerates thermal degradation and can cause irreversible cell damage.
prognosis.reasoning: The four adjacent cells are already 2.7‑2.8 °C above the array median, indicating a bypass‑diode fault. With clear skies and peak irradiance of 966 W/m², cell temperature is projected to reach 67.5 °C, exceeding the 65 °C dose limit. Continued operation will accumulate the 5‑hour dose budget within the next 72 h, leading to further loss. Intervention before 14:00 prevents irreversible degradation.

recommendation.primaryAction: Replace cracked cell/module and restore string performance
steps: Isolate string B-17-S3 and perform lockout/tagout on inverter INV-B
Remove module B2-07 from array B-17 and inspect row 2 cells 3‑6 for the cracked cell
Replace the damaged cell (or the entire module B2-07) ensuring proper solder joints, sealing, and re‑install the module
Re‑energize inverter INV-B, measure string voltage/current to verify the -58.4% shortfall is corrected and perform thermal imaging to confirm no hot band remains
recommendation.costOfDelayNote: High risk – projected loss of 3.07 MWh over 72 h; delay beyond 14:00 could exceed thermal‑degradation threshold of 65 °C
